To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the global convergence of work systems in MNCs is shaped by the institutional contexts of the home country of the MNC and of the host country of the subsidiary.

the global players in the lift and escalator industry have a strong global orientation, but they have to adapt to the national context, and this adaptation is shaped by the national institutional context.
globalization and national diversity intertwine and that there are no best practices of globalization in MNCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the `middle ground' of international business research, the `meso level' of the subsidiary.
the question of how the global and the national intertwine in change management processes in MNCs' subsidiaries.
the `globalization' of the MNC as a social organization and the interplay of global and local effects in shaping the work systems of MNCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no best way of globalising in MNCs and that the effects of globalization are not uniform across the subsidiaries of the same MNC.
the global players in the industry have developed a global strategy of work system management, which is, however, adapted to the different institutional contexts of their national subsidiaries.
globalization and national institutional context are not mutually exclusive, but rather interdependent and mutually reinforcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
global and national effects are not mutually exclusive but rather intertwined in the process of globalization.
the global players in the lift industry have been successful in implementing global change management processes in their subsidiaries.
global convergence in MNCs is not a linear process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the institutional environment of a country is a key driver of the way in which MNCs organize their work systems at the local level.
the institutional context matters for the way MNCs organize work systems in their subsidiaries.
the national context is not just a background factor, but a crucial element in shaping the work systems in MNCs.
